Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's reply! The Umpire walk out and the India Under-19 fielders take their positions. Ashiqur Rahman Shibli and Jishan Alam are the openers for Bangladesh Under-19. Raj Limbani has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. 'Let's play' says the Umpire.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

As both teams retreat to the dressing room, Bangladesh would likely carry a slightly more contented demeanour, having succeeded in restricting India to a manageable total. However, the Indians, armed with a formidable bowling attack and adept spinners in their arsenal, are poised to be optimistic about their chances on this pitch. The stage is set for an exciting second inning that will be coming up shortly, so stick around.

The Head Coach of Bangladesh Under-19, Stuart Law is down for a chat. He says this ground is known to be a high-scoring ground and to keep India down to 251 is a top effort by the bowlers. He then talks about the conditions and says that the spinners bowled exceptionally well. He then appreciates Maruf Mridha and says he has developed pretty well, has worked very hard and is now reaping the rewards. He further says that the wicket doesn't change a lot here and with that target on the board, the batters will have to stick to the process and gameplan to tackle the Indian bowling attack.

Opting to bowl first after winning the toss, Bangladesh Under-19 initiated early breakthroughs, with Maruf Mridha sending Arshin Kulkarni and Musheer Khan back to the pavilion inexpensively. However, India's middle overs surged without any further losses, causing Bangladesh to momentarily lose their grip on proceedings. A life for Adarsh Singh cost Bangladesh a lot of runs as he was dismissed early on in his innings by Md Iqbal Hasan Emon but was off a No Ball. A resurgence for Bangladesh came after the second drinks break, as they regrouped and bowled with renewed vigour. Md. Rohanat Doullah Borson emerged as a key figure, breaking the crucial partnership between Uday Saharan and Adarsh Singh, eventually claiming both set batters. The spinners then tightened their lines, preventing the Indian batters from settling in. The pick of the bowlers was Maruf Mridha who further delivered his career-best figures and got his five-fer knocking the Indian lower middle order. This collective effort allowed Bangladesh to curtail India's total to 251, thwarting what seemed like a potential 30-40 run surplus at one stage.

India Under-19 do not get the desired finish but they do get to 251, which looks like a competitive total! The defending champions witnessed a bit of a collapse with the bat, leaving them slightly disappointed with the late developments in their innings. Following the early setbacks, Adarsh Singh and Skipper Uday Saharan demonstrated resilience against the new ball attack, navigating through the challenging phase and orchestrating meticulously paced innings. Their partnership flourished into a commendable 116-run alliance, with both batters reaching well-deserved half-centuries. Post the break of the key partnership, the latter part of India's innings saw a swift turnaround. Thanks to quick-fire contributions from Aravelly Rao and Sachin Dhas, India Under-19 could reach a fighting total despite the stumbling blocks encountered earlier.

Finishes it off with a well-executed yorker, right at the base of the off-stump, Sachin Dhas gets his bat down in time and squeezes it out to backward point for a single. Just the 5 runs off the final over and India Under-19 end up with 251 on the board!
